newsitem.title: USA: Castle Energy net off on new accounting.
newsitem.headline: Castle Energy net off on new accounting.

text.p: Castle Energy Corp said Tuesday the drop in its second quarter, ended March 31, earnings was attributed primarily to a different accounting treatment for income taxes.
The company reported earnings of $2.9 million, or $0.50 per share, for the latest quarter. This compared with earnings of $5.1 million, or $0.77 per share, for the quarter ended March 31, 1996.

For that quarter, the company noted, a zero tax provision was recorded, because the company had substantial operating loss carryforwards, but had not yet recorded a deferred tax asset applicable to such carryforwards.

For the latest quarter, a 36 percent tax provision was necessary because the company had recorded a $7.7 million deferred tax asset at Sept. 30, 1996, based upon anticipated taxable income to be generated by its natural gas marketing and transmission business.
The 36 percent tax provision in 1997 represents the amortization of such deferred tax asset.
The company said it expects to record a similar 36 percent tax provision in the future although it expects to actually pay taxes at a two percent rate.
It said pre-tax income for the 1997 quarter was $4,545,000 versus $5,134,000 for the 1966 quarter.
